summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted with acute-on-chronic left upper quadrant abdominal pain and nausea, lasting four days, which improved with eating. Initial evaluation showed no signs of infection, obstruction, or surgical pathology on labs or imaging. She was managed conservatively with resumption of proton pump inhibitor, H2 blocker, and sucralfate, scheduled acetaminophen, bowel regimen, and loperamide for diarrhea. Stool testing was negative for C. difficile. Pyridostigmine was discontinued due to potential gastrointestinal side effects and negative neurologic workup for myasthenia gravis. The bariatric surgery team recommended medical management and referral to chronic pain service for presumed visceral hyperalgesia. Pain improved, and she was discharged home in stable condition with follow-up plans.
problems: Major depressive disorder, single episode, unspecified
Epilepsy, unspecified, not intractable, without status epilepticus
History of roux-en-Y gastric bypass, status post open reversal
